target_claim_or_section: ADV-002 / CLM-010: temporal archive of IRS releases 'cannot be recreated retroactively'; 'the only one that strictly cannot be bought later'
challenge: The BMF half of the archive already exists outside Unbound. The Urban Institute's NCCS publishes raw, unmodified monthly IRS BMF releases (raw/bmf/YYYY-MM-BMF.csv), with a transformed series from 2023-06 to 2026-07 and harmonized vintages back to 1989, though the series has gaps. The package's own change-rate evidence (charity-network 06 section 2.1) was computed from this 'NCCS mirror of IRS monthly files'. Candid says it pings the IRS every 20 minutes, downloads BMF, Pub 78 and revocation files on change, and keeps revocation and reinstatement history on the record. ICPSR also holds BMF extracts. The auto-revocation file is itself cumulative, with effective dates, posting dates and reinstatements. That leaves Pub 78 snapshots and fine-grained provenance as the only parts that are plausibly scarce.
evidence: urbaninstitute.github.io/nccs/catalogs/catalog-bmf.html (raw monthly archive; legacy 1989-2022); urbaninstitute.github.io/nccs/datasets/pub78 (no Pub 78 history); developer.candid.org/reference/faqs-charity-check ('ping the IRS website every 20 minutes'; revocation and reinstatement kept 'for research purposes'); charity-network 06 s2.1 [REG-012] cites the NCCS mirror. Wayback CDX was blocked from this session (UNVERIFIED).
proposed_change: Downgrade ADV-002 from 'moderate advantage' to 'hygiene / parity for BMF; possible narrow edge only for Pub 78 snapshots plus hash-level provenance'. Change CLM-010 to state that NCCS, Candid and ICPSR already hold BMF history. Add an evidence-gap item to check Internet Archive and GivingTuesday holdings of Pub 78 and the revocation files.

target_claim_or_section: RP-07 evidence_expiry_share base 0.10 (5-20%) vs 04 s4 expiry periods (bank 24 months; website 12 months)
challenge: The parameter contradicts the architecture's own expiry rules. If every charity in use has a bank letter that expires every 24 months and a website check that expires every 12 months, expiry events run at about 150% of charities a year, not 10%. At 20k charities and 5 minutes each, that is about 2,500 hours against about 167 hours. The gap is about $155k a year at $67.69 an hour, which is more than the whole RA-1 run cost. Bank re-verification is also rarely a 5-minute task, because it needs contact with the charity or a vendor.
evidence: 04 s4: 'bank verification 24 months; website check 12 months'; registry-parameters.csv RP-07 0.1 ASSUMPTION; RP-08 5 min ASSUMPTION; RP-14 $67.69/h
proposed_change: Derive RP-07 from the expiry table: sum over evidence types of the share of charities holding the evidence divided by the validity in years. Separate bank re-verification, priced as a vendor fee or charity outreach, from website checks. Rerun RA-0 to RA-7 and restate the $90-120k floor.

target_claim_or_section: RP-02 4% eligibility-relevant change rate (basis: 405 adverse-candidate BMF changes per month plus 'monitoring 4% status events')
challenge: The 4% counts IRS status events, but the package adds several monitoring feeds whose alerts are not in that number. These are the full trade.gov CSL (26,339 rows), the UK, UN and EU lists, SAM exclusions, FAC going-concern and material-weakness flags, the CA AG 'may not operate' list, and state corporate dissolution. Name-only screening of organisation names against roughly 26k export-control and sanctions rows produces false positives at every delta. OFAC alone updates 110-130 days a year, and charity names such as 'Al-...', 'Relief', 'Foundation for ...' or 'Islamic ...' match often. Those dispositions are exception work. The 4% also comes from one month of BMF diffs (06 rates it Medium for annualisation) and the August revocation batch, so peak load is far above the mean.
evidence: 02 s1-2 (CSL, SAM, FAC added as monitoring signals); charity-network 06 s2.1-2.2 (one month; about 70% of revocations post in August; OFAC update days); registry-parameters RP-02 basis
proposed_change: Split RP-02 into (a) IRS status events, (b) screening alerts from name matching and (c) FAC, SAM and state flags. Measure (b) by screening a real 20k charity list against the CSL and SDN with the intended matcher. Model the August revocation peak for staffing, not just the annual mean.

target_claim_or_section: RP-03 45-minute mean exception (30-60) with 20-30% deterministic auto-resolution
challenge: The basis is an assumption carried over from a sibling package ('charity-network ECO C0 45 min'), not a measurement. In practice the exception mix has a heavy tail. Catholic parishes need an OCD page plus a cover page. Other church and subordinate cases need the central organisation to confirm. Successor and merger cases need documents and sponsor approval. Foreign equivalency, Type III supporting organisations, DBA and fiscal-sponsored project binding, and payment-destination mismatches also need outreach. Many of these involve waiting on the charity for days and several contacts, so hands-on time often runs to hours. A 45-minute mean is plausible for screening false positives and poor for the rest. Section 5 then makes 45 minutes a condition the operator 'must demonstrate', which is circular, because the cost conclusion already rests on it.
evidence: registry-parameters RP-03 basis; 02 s3 identity table; trackA-notes s2.7 (OCD cover-page requirement for USCCB GEN 0928); 05 s5 item 2
proposed_change: Model exceptions by class, each with its own minutes and elapsed-days distribution, using a lognormal or triangular with a fat right tail. Report the cost at P90 handling time. Label the 45-minute mean UNVERIFIED until a timed sample of real exceptions exists.

target_claim_or_section: 'Every input a sponsor needs for the legal minimum ... is free and redistributable'; 'Yes for determinations' (03 s5; 02 s4)
challenge: This is true for IRS status and sanctions, but not for the full DAF determination. Section 170(c)(1) governmental grantees (public school districts, public universities, municipalities, tribal governments) are eligible but appear in neither Pub 78 nor the BMF. Non-applicant churches are absent too. Section 4966 and 4967 rules on Type I and III supporting organisations, and the Type III functionally-integrated versus non-functionally-integrated split, turn on control by donors or disqualified persons. Public data cannot show that, so a certification from the charity is needed. Organisations recognised too recently to appear in Pub 78 or the BMF are missing as well (Candid's 'advanced status' comes from determination letters charities upload). Foreign grantees need equivalency or expenditure responsibility. Free data supports status determinations, not eligibility determinations.
evidence: developer.candid.org FAQ ('advanced status' from determination letters, not in the API); Candid field docs (FED/government deductibility type; church messages); 02 s3 (foreign equivalency left to the sponsor); IRC 4966(d)(4) and 4967 (statutory)
proposed_change: Restate the claim as 'free data suffices for IRS status, revocation, sanctions and exclusion facts'. Add governmental units, new determinations and supporting-organisation control certifications as named coverage holes with an evidence class (charity-provided or certified). Add their exception volume to RP-05.

target_claim_or_section: s6: charity intelligence could be a product as an 'eligibility evidence service' (status, screening and change history via API)
challenge: The price ceiling is already low. Candid Charity Check starts at $2,750 a year. Its 40+ fields already combine BMF, Pub 78, Internal Revenue Bulletin, auto-revocation, OFAC SDN and 501(p) status, a subordinate-inheritance indicator, church messages and a California AG and FTB endpoint, with a bulk tier of 25 organisations per call and timestamped PDF evidence. Pactman Nonprofit Check Plus is free up to 200 checks a month. Treasury Do Not Pay offers federal agencies Pub 78 continuous monitoring at no cost. The differentiators left are change history and event push, and Candid's lack of a monitoring endpoint can be closed cheaply. The 'incumbent paid market' line understates this. On the evidence, the market is a commodity sold at a few thousand dollars a year.
evidence: developer.candid.org/llms.txt (Charity Check, Bulk, PDF and California endpoints); developer.candid.org/reference/interpret-charity-check-data-fields (OFAC Status, Pub78 Indicator 2 = subordinate, church messages); search results for Candid pricing 'starting at $2,750'; Pactman Nonprofit Check Plus listing (free 200/month); fiscal.treasury.gov irs-teos-qrc.pdf (Do Not Pay continuous monitoring)
proposed_change: Add a competitor price table for Candid, Pactman, Do Not Pay and Every.org/OrgHunter. Test HYP-007 against a willingness-to-pay ceiling of about $3-10k a year per sponsor for status and screening. Treat ER-1 as unattractive unless replayable decision evidence with audit acceptance is the thing being sold.

target_claim_or_section: RA-5 commercial licence $60k base ($25-150k; RP-12 'price not published, UNKNOWN')
challenge: The package's own source register records Candid APIs 'From $2,750/yr (vendor list price per repo)', and Charity Check pricing is published as starting at $2,750. That is an order of magnitude below the RA-5 base, so the conclusion that commercial enrichment is 'the most expensive single-sponsor option' is driven by an assumption that contradicts the register. Enterprise or bulk redistribution licences may cost more, but the use the model assumes (enriching one sponsor's own decisions) is the low-tier use case.
evidence: data/registers/charity-data-sources.csv row CANDID ('From $2,750/yr'); registry-parameters RP-12; registry-alternatives RA-5 commercial_licence_usd 60000
proposed_change: Set the RP-12 low value at about $2.75k and the base from a tiered quote assumption, then rerun RA-5. If RA-5 then becomes competitive with RA-1, note that it buys Candid's DBA, alias and advanced-status data, which addresses the identity holes in 02 s3.

target_claim_or_section: Identity table (02 s3): 'EIN reuse and mergers - BMF silent removal on revocation; no tombstone'; group subordinates as a roster problem; DBA via alias table
challenge: This misdescribes the hard identity problems. The IRS does not reassign EINs, so the real failures run the other way. Conversions, mergers and reincorporations produce new EINs for the 'same' charity. Some EINs are shared by many operating units: fiscal-sponsored projects (the package counts 20,566), chapters, and subordinates who list the central organisation's EIN. Revocations are not tombstone-less either, because the cumulative auto-revocation file is the tombstone. The dominant DAF identity task is mapping a donor's free-text name or DBA to an EIN. Pub 78 carries no DBAs, and the BMF truncates names, so this depends on alias data that only self-reported aggregators such as Candid hold. The 800-hour entity-resolution establishment budget and 'candidate links, never auto-merge' do not size this work.
evidence: 02 s3; charity-network 06 s2.2 (revocation file with reinstatement dates = history); Treasury TEOS QRC ('If an organization uses a doing business as (DBA) name, that name will not be listed in the PUB 78 Data'); 02 s1 (Fiscal Sponsor Directory 20,566 projects)
proposed_change: Rewrite the identity table around (1) donor name or DBA to EIN, (2) one EIN for many units (fiscal sponsor, chapter, subordinate), (3) one charity across many EINs (succession). Measure the hit rate of name-to-EIN matching on a sample of real donor grant requests before fixing the RP-05 exception rate.

target_claim_or_section: '0 of 237,380 c3 subordinates appear in Pub 78'; churches and subordinates are a 'structural hole that no public source fills'; 'only proprietary OCD and ECFA lists exist'
challenge: This overstates the problem. The 237k subordinates are in the BMF with a group exemption number and affiliation codes, and the central organisation's annual roster submission keeps that listing current. Candid's Pub78 Indicator = 2 shows a vendor automating subordinate eligibility from the central organisation's record. The genuine hole is narrower: non-applicant churches, plus large groups like USCCB GEN 0928 whose subordinates are not individually listed. The case also cuts the other way for the package. If subordinate status can be largely automated from the BMF, it does not justify the exception-labour assumptions. If it cannot, the 4% and 45-minute figures undercount it. The package uses it both ways (a structural hole in 02, absent from RP-02 and RP-03).
evidence: developer.candid.org/reference/interpret-charity-check-data-fields (Pub78 Indicator 2 'subordinate ... inherits its data from the central organization'; GROUP deductibility); charity-network 06 field counts (GROUP and AFFILIATION changes); trackA-notes s2.7
proposed_change: Quantify the BMF-listed subordinates (automatable via GEN) separately from unlisted church and Catholic units (evidence workflow). Estimate the share of DAF grant volume going to each, for example from a sample of donor-advised fund grant reports, and feed the unlisted share into the exception model.

target_claim_or_section: Licensing classes: state data treated as public domain or 'Yes' independent; shared registry may hold 'public-domain and open-licensed facts' only
challenge: 17 USC 105 covers federal works only. State AG registries (CA AG 'may not operate', NY), state corporate registries other than Colorado's explicit public-domain dedication, and NASCO material have state-specific terms, copyright claims or paid-bulk contracts (GA $1,000, IN $9.5k+). The package already marks several of these UNKNOWN, yet 02 counts the CA list as 'supports automation' and RA-4 assumes a shared layer. The shared registry's actual dependency is also undisclosed: the package's own change-rate measurement used the NCCS mirror, whose licence was not recorded.
evidence: 03 s1 table (no row for CA AG or NY AG terms); 02 s1 (CA list 'supports automation'); charity-network 06 [REG-012] NCCS mirror; NCCS catalog page shows no licence text
proposed_change: Add a licence row per state source actually planned, at minimum CA AG and NY AG. Record the NCCS licence or ingest directly from the IRS for any production replay. Keep state facts out of the shared layer until terms are confirmed by counsel (OQ-007).
